title: When the Garden Burns
premise: Paloma Galloway, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, hides her gift behind a stall of harmless charms until the crown's witch-hunt flushes magic users into the streets. When a dying stranger presses a debt-token into his hand — a claim on a soul sold twelve years ago to the court beneath the mountain — Paloma realizes it is his own soul, traded by his mother to save his life. Descending into the buried court, he must choose between the oath that binds his sword to the crown and the truth that the crown itself brokered his soul. In the end he burns the garden of oaths that feeds the court's power, reclaims his soul at the cost of his gift, and returns to the surface as winter breaks — belonging to no crown, but finally to himself and the found family who followed him down.
about_author: Mara Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about oaths, debts, and the people brave enough to break both.

chapters.title: Charms for a Magicless City
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He sells a love charm that secretly does nothing, hiding his swordspeaker gift behind sleight of hand. A city crier announces the crown's hunt for the gifted. Emotional beat: the quiet dread of a hiding place about to fail.

chapters.title: The Dying Man at the Door
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A stranger, hunted and bleeding, staggers into his shop and presses a bone debt-token into his hand with a warning: the court beneath the mountain keeps what is sold. Guards arrive; the man dies. Paloma flees. Beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Token Says
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with a flashback. Reading the token, he learns it names him — a soul sold twelve years ago by his mother. He remembers the oath his mother made him swear. Beat: betrayal cracking the foundation of his identity.

chapters.title: The Hunt Comes to Ashrow Lane
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Crown inquisitors sweep the district, and his neighbor Tamsin, a hedge-healer, is taken. Paloma uses his gift openly for the first time in years to break her free. Beat: the exhilaration and terror of choosing a side.

chapters.title: An Oath Is a Chain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He examines the oath binding his sword to the crown and realizes it is the leash the hunt will use to find him. He cannot break it without dying. Beat: claustrophobia of inherited obligation.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Buried Roads
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin brings him to Odd Wren, a disgraced cartographer who maps passages into the court beneath the mountain. Wren agrees to help — for a debt of her own. Beat: the first fragile spark of found alliance.

chapters.title: Down the Stair That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Paloma, Tamsin, and Wren descend through a sealed stair. The mountain's magic tests them, showing each a temptation. Paloma sees his mother alive. Beat: longing weaponized against the traveler.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They reach the underground court, beautiful and wrong: a court of the sold and the sold-from, lit by a burning garden of oaths. Paloma recognizes his own soul among the kept things. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Sold Souls
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Keeper, a courteous ancient thing, confirms his soul's price and offers a trade: his gift, freely given, in exchange for the soul's release. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin secretly negotiates with the court's under-clerk to buy information about the garden's heart, paying with memories of her dead sister. Beat: grief spent as currency, and the cost of loyalty.

chapters.title: Wren's Map Ends Here
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals she was born in the buried court and sold upward as a child; her maps were always a way home. She refuses to leave without the other sold children. Beat: inheritance as wound, not gift.

chapters.title: The Crown's Envoy
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The crown's chief inquisitor arrives below — the crown has always known the court exists and trades with it. He offers Paloma pardon for betraying his companions. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made explicit and personal.

chapters.title: A Sword Speaks True
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The inquisitor invokes Paloma's oath, forcing his sword to turn on Tamsin. Paloma speaks against his own blade — the one act a swordspeaker cannot do — and the oath begins to crack. Beat: defiance at terrible personal cost.

chapters.title: The Garden of Oaths
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Guided by Tamsin's bought knowledge, they reach the garden where every oath ever sworn to the crown burns as fuel. Paloma understands: his mother's oath, his oath, all of it feeds the court. Beat: revelation as liberation and terror.

chapters.title: What My Mother Sold
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, flashback-heavy. He confronts his mother's memory held in the garden and learns she sold his soul to buy the city a decade of peace — and that the crown broke the bargain. Beat: forgiveness without absolution.

chapters.title: Fire Needs a Speaker
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The plan forms: only a swordspeaker's oath, spoken and then renounced, can set the garden burning out of control. Wren maps the escape route while the court's hunters close in. Beat: hope assembled from scraps.

chapters.title: The Renunciation
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Before the Keeper and the inquisitor, Paloma swears a new oath and immediately breaks it, igniting the garden. The court begins to collapse; sold souls stir free. Beat: climax — sacrifice as the price of truth.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Last Ledger
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The dying Keeper offers him a final choice: keep his gift and lose his soul, or take his soul and lose the gift forever. Paloma chooses himself. Beat: the theme of inheritance resolved by refusal.

chapters.title: Running Before the Fall
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The escape through collapsing galleries as Wren leads the freed children upward. Tamsin spends her last bought memory to hold a door open. Beat: loyalty proven in action, grief transmuted into love.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's End
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The inquisitor, oath-bound to a burning crown, refuses rescue and is consumed by the garden's fire. Paloma, giftless, faces him with only a sword and a truth. Beat: the hunt ends; the hunter is unmasked as the hunted.

chapters.title: Winter Breaks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They surface into the first thaw. The city's magic ban falters as the crown's oath-fuel is gone. Paloma, ordinary at last, reopens his stall — and this time the charms are only charms. Beat: quiet, earned peace.

chapters.title: When the Garden Burns
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, epilogue. Wren's new maps open trade with the freed court below; Tamsin plants a real garden over the old stair. Paloma writes his mother's name in the ashes and lets it go. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited.
